title: Universal enriched localization on functor categories
statement:
Fix universes large enough that the categories and diagram shapes in this statement are small. Let $\mathcal V=\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$ be the symmetric monoidal enhanced localization of unbounded cochain complexes of abelian groups at quasi-isomorphisms, with derived tensor; complexes and quasi-isomorphisms have the convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. A $\mathcal V$-enriched infinity category has mapping objects in $\mathcal V$, associative composition and identity maps with all their coherent homotopies. A relative enriched category is such a category $\mathcal C$ together with a collection $W$ of underlying degree-zero morphisms. An enriched localization is an enriched functor $q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[W^{-1}]$ inverting $W$ that is universal in the following sense.

Such localizations exist, and for every $\mathcal V$-enriched infinity category $\mathcal E$, restriction along $q$ gives an equivalence of enhanced functor categories
$$q^*:\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V}(\mathcal C[W^{-1}],\mathcal E)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathcal V,W}(\mathcal C,\mathcal E),$$
where the right side is the full enhanced subcategory on functors sending $W$ to equivalences. In particular restriction is fully faithful on mapping objects, hence on transformations and every higher homotopy between them. The assertion also applies to relative differential graded categories, using their derived enrichment, and to opposites. An enriched functor of relative enriched categories preserving the distinguished maps induces an enriched functor of these localizations; enriched natural transformations of such functors and specified coherent diagrams of transformations induce the corresponding transformations and diagrams. A relative functor whose localized functor is an equivalence can be inverted for all these restrictions.

For finitely many relative enriched categories $(\mathcal C_i,W_i)$ and an enriched functor $H$ in their variables, the same assertion applies to multivariable functors which send $W_i$ to equivalences separately in each variable, with other inputs fixed. Restriction along the localizations is an equivalence of these enhanced categories of multivariable functors. These equivalences are compatible with substitution of functors, composition and identity transformations, and passage to any small homotopy coherent diagram of the specified functors and transformations. The extension space over a fixed functor or specified diagram, including its specified restriction, is contractible; a transformation is an equivalence precisely when all its components are equivalences.
